evaluator: model (Claude Sonnet 5.5), NOT a human evaluator
input: qualitative_sheets.md only (titles, years, genres, first 220 characters of the plot, and the model's general film knowledge)
blindness: Imperfect. Before this evaluation the evaluator had seen the automatic aggregates and per-case metric deltas of the three variants (ab_summary-style numbers), but NOT which label X/Y/Z maps to which variant: qualitative_key.json and ab_summary.md were not opened. Lists that are identical across labels were scored identically.
scale: per item: r = relevance to the request text; p = closeness to the liked film(s); n = resemblance to the film(s) to avoid; each in {0, 0.5, 1}; null when the sheet gives no liked/avoided film. defects = items whose title/year/genre are not a coherent film record (e.g. a file path used as title).
list_rules: P (pertinenza) and V (vicinanza): mean of r / p >= 0.7 -> 2, >= 0.3 -> 1, else 0. A (assenza del tratto da evitare): 0 if any n = 1 or mean n >= 0.4; 1 if any n >= 0.5 or mean n >= 0.15; else 2. F (fatti): 0 defects -> 2, 1 -> 1, >= 2 -> 0.
limits: Single evaluator, a model; plot snippets are truncated to 220 characters so some judgments rely on prior knowledge of the films; the three-level item judgments are coarse. Indicative evidence, not a statistical result.
